patient.name: Ayaan Hussain
patient.setting: GP surgery, then paediatric oncology ward
patient.complaint: Three weeks of pallor, tiredness, bruising and leg pains
background: Two sore throats in the last month
Previously well; immunisations up to date
Lives with his parents and baby sister in Tower Hamlets

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' from age plus film: child with marrow failure and HSM (ALL), elderly with Auer rods (AML), massive spleen (CML), incidental lymphocytosis with smudge cells (CLL).

points: Ayaan, 4, brought to the GP by his dad.
Three weeks: **pale, tired**, no longer wants to play.
**Bruises** on his legs and back nobody can explain.
Two throat infections this month; wakes with **leg pains**.

steps.lead: Ayaan's pallor, bruising and infections are **bone marrow failure**: the marrow is full of malignant white cells, so normal cells are crowded out.
Ayaan is 4, right in the **ALL peak of 2–5 years**. An adult over 65 would make you think AML; an older man with an incidental high WCC, CLL.

points: Pale, with bruises and a few **petechiae** on his chest.
Rubbery nodes in his neck and groins.
Soft systolic murmur (flow murmur from anaemia).

visual.title: Ayaan's abdomen
visual.caption: Hepatosplenomegaly from leukaemic infiltration. Massive splenomegaly alone in an adult points to CML.

steps.lead: Ayaan has the marrow failure triad plus **lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly**: classic ALL.

steps.q: Which single feature in Ayaan's story most worries you about leukaemia rather than a viral illness?
steps.r: Bruising plus pallor means **two cell lines** are failing: platelets and red cells. That needs a same-day FBC.

steps.lead: Boys with ALL are checked for **testicular involvement** (poor prognosis). In an adult with DIC and t(15;17), think **APML**.
Ayaan is at risk of **infection, bleeding and anaemia**. In CLL, also watch for **autoimmune haemolysis** and **Richter's transformation**.

steps.text: Do not send a pale, bruised child home with 'viral illness'. NICE: an **FBC within 48 hours** and **same-day referral** if leukaemia is suspected.

investigation.exam: Expect 'diagnostic investigation' (bone marrow biopsy), 'first-line' (FBC and film; flow cytometry in CLL) or 'most likely film finding' (Auer rods, smudge cells).

steps.title: Ayaan's same-day FBC
steps.text: High total WCC, but made of blasts: the normal cells are all low.

steps.lead: Ayaan's FBC and film are first-line: anaemia, low neutrophils and platelets with **lymphoblasts**. AML would show **Auer rods**; CLL **smudge cells**.

steps.text: A **high WCC** does not mean good immunity: Ayaan's white cells are blasts, and his **neutrophils are 0.4**.

steps.q: Which test is the gold standard to confirm Ayaan's diagnosis?
steps.r: **Bone marrow aspirate and trephine** confirms leukaemia and gives the subtype and cytogenetics.

steps.lead: Ayaan has a **bone marrow biopsy** under general anaesthetic: it confirms B-cell ALL and sends cells for cytogenetics.

visual.title: Blasts in Ayaan's marrow
visual.label: Ayaan 86%
visual.caption: At least 20% blasts in the marrow defines acute leukaemia.

steps.text: CLL is the exception: **flow cytometry of peripheral blood** is the first-line test, showing a clonal B-cell population.

Leukaemia
rows: Myeloid cells at all stages, basophils

management.exam: Expect same-day referral for a child, imatinib for CML, watch and wait for early CLL and immediate IV antibiotics for neutropenic sepsis.

steps.q: The GP's FBC shows blasts. What is the most appropriate next step for Ayaan?
o: Oral antibiotics and review in a week
steps.r: Suspected leukaemia in a child: **urgent same-day referral** to paediatrics.

steps.lead: Ayaan is admitted the same day and starts **induction chemotherapy**. His blasts are **hyperdiploid**, a good sign. CML would get **imatinib** instead.

steps.title: Ayaan's first week
nodes: IV fluids and allopurinol to prevent tumour lysis
steps.caption: Cells dying fast release potassium, phosphate and urate: prevent tumour lysis syndrome.

steps.title: Day 2 bloods
steps.text: High K, phosphate and urate with low calcium: tumour lysis syndrome.
Tumour lysis syndrome: **high** potassium, phosphate and urate, **low** calcium. Prevent with IV fluids and allopurinol or **rasburicase**.

steps.lead: Ayaan needs **red cell and platelet transfusions** and infection care. An older patient with stable CLL might simply **watch and wait**.

visual.title: Ayaan's neutrophils during induction
visual.caption: Neutrophils hit their lowest around day 12, when Ayaan spikes a fever.

steps.lead: Fever plus neutrophils of 0.1 is **neutropenic sepsis**: cultures and **IV broad-spectrum antibiotics** (piperacillin-tazobactam) within **1 hour**.

visual.title: Neutrophil count
visual.label: Ayaan 0.1
visual.caption: Fever with neutrophils ≤0.5: treat as neutropenic sepsis, do not wait for results.

science.exam: Expect translocations and mechanisms: t(9;22) BCR-ABL and imatinib, t(15;17) and DIC, why marrow infiltration causes the triad.

steps.lead: One malignant clone took over Ayaan's marrow, crowding out red cell, myeloid and platelet precursors: hence **anaemia, infection and bleeding**.

steps.title: From clone to symptoms
nodes: Clonal blasts proliferate, fail to mature

steps.q: Ayaan's cytogenetics are checked for t(9;22). Which leukaemia is defined by it?
steps.r: **t(9;22) BCR-ABL** (Philadelphia chromosome) defines CML. Ayaan's ALL is Philadelphia-negative.

steps.lead: Ayaan is **Philadelphia-negative**. In CML, BCR-ABL is a permanently switched-on tyrosine kinase, which is why **imatinib** works.
APML's **PML-RARA** fusion freezes cells as promyelocytes, whose granules trigger **DIC**: a haematological emergency Ayaan does not have.
Ayaan's film shows lymphoblasts, not **Auer rods** (AML) or **smudge cells** (fragile CLL lymphocytes crushed on the slide).

glossary.ALL: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia: the commonest childhood cancer, peaking at 2 to 5 years.
glossary.AML: Acute myeloid leukaemia: mostly over 65s; Auer rods on the film.
glossary.CML: Chronic myeloid leukaemia: defined by the Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22); massive splenomegaly.
glossary.CLL: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia: older men, often an incidental lymphocytosis; smudge cells.
glossary.APML: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia: AML subtype with t(15;17), prone to DIC.
glossary.Blasts: Immature white blood cell precursors; at least 20% in the marrow means acute leukaemia.
glossary.Lymphoblasts: Immature lymphoid blasts, seen in ALL.
glossary.Myeloblasts: Immature myeloid blasts, seen in AML.
glossary.Promyelocyte: Myeloid precursor between myeloblast and myelocyte; accumulates in APML.
glossary.Auer rods: Rod-shaped clumps of granule material in myeloblast cytoplasm; a hallmark of AML.
glossary.Smudge cells: Ruptured fragile lymphocytes on a blood film; typical of CLL.
glossary.Pancytopenia: Low red cells, white cells and platelets together.
glossary.Bone marrow failure: Marrow cannot make enough normal blood cells, causing anaemia, infection and bleeding.
glossary.Bone marrow biopsy: Aspirate and trephine sample of marrow; gold standard for diagnosing leukaemia.
glossary.Flow cytometry: Laser test that identifies cells by surface markers; first-line for CLL.
glossary.Cytogenetics: Study of chromosomes in cancer cells to find translocations that guide prognosis and treatment.
glossary.Philadelphia chromosome: Shortened chromosome 22 from t(9;22), carrying the BCR-ABL fusion gene.
glossary.BCR-ABL: Fusion gene making a permanently active tyrosine kinase; drives CML.
glossary.PML-RARA: Fusion gene from t(15;17) that blocks promyelocyte maturation in APML.
glossary.Tyrosine kinase: Enzyme that switches on cell signalling; overactive in CML.
glossary.Imatinib: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting BCR-ABL; first-line in CML.
glossary.Hyperdiploidy: Extra chromosomes in leukaemic cells; a good prognostic sign in ALL.
glossary.Induction chemotherapy: First intensive phase of chemotherapy aiming to put leukaemia into remission.
glossary.DIC: Disseminated intravascular coagulation: widespread clotting that consumes platelets and factors, causing bleeding.
glossary.Neutropenic sepsis: Fever or sepsis with neutrophils at or below 0.5; needs IV antibiotics within 1 hour.
glossary.Piperacillin-tazobactam: Broad-spectrum IV antibiotic used first-line for neutropenic sepsis.
glossary.Tumour lysis syndrome: Rapid tumour cell death releasing potassium, phosphate and urate, with low calcium, risking AKI and arrhythmia.
glossary.Rasburicase: Recombinant urate oxidase that breaks down uric acid; prevents and treats tumour lysis.
glossary.Allopurinol: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor that reduces uric acid production; used to prevent tumour lysis syndrome.
glossary.Richter's transformation: CLL turning into an aggressive high-grade lymphoma.
glossary.Warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia: Antibodies against red cells active at body temperature; associated with CLL.
glossary.Hepatosplenomegaly: Enlargement of both liver and spleen.
glossary.Leukoerythroblastic: Blood film with immature white and red cells, from marrow infiltration or stress.
glossary.Petechiae: Pinpoint red spots from capillary bleeding, typical of low platelets.
glossary.Watch and wait: Monitoring without treatment until disease causes symptoms; used in early CLL.
glossary.Leukostasis: Very high blast counts clogging small vessels, causing headache, visual change and breathlessness.
glossary.Priapism: Prolonged painful erection; can occur from leukostasis in leukaemia.
glossary.Down syndrome: Trisomy 21; raises the risk of acute leukaemia.
glossary.MPO: Myeloperoxidase: enzyme in myeloid granules; positive staining marks myeloid blasts.

technique.stem: An 80 year old man attends a routine GP appointment and says he has felt more tired than usual. He has no weight loss or night sweats. Examination shows small, painless lymph nodes in both axillae. His full blood count shows a raised white cell count and the film shows smudge cells.
technique.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

steps.x: Diagnosis from age and film.
Elderly man, near-incidental finding, lymphocytosis, smudge cells.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia**.

elim: Acute illness with marrow failure and Auer rods; not this.
Raised neutrophil lineage, basophils and massive splenomegaly; lymphocytes are not the problem.
Young adults with lymph node mass and Reed-Sternberg cells.
Young person with sore throat; atypical lymphocytes, not smudge cells.

steps.x: **B. Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia.** Rule: older man + incidental lymphocytosis + smudge cells = CLL.

technique.stem: A 71 year old woman has 3 weeks of tiredness, recurrent chest infections and gum bleeding. Her full blood count shows pancytopenia with circulating blasts.
technique.q: Which is the most likely finding on her blood film?

steps.x: A 'most likely finding' question: diagnose first.

clues: recurrent chest infections and gum bleeding
steps.x: Older adult, rapid marrow failure, blasts: **AML**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: AML film: **Auer rods**.

elim: G6PD deficiency.
Seen on lymph node biopsy in Hodgkin lymphoma, not the blood film.
CLL, a slow, often incidental disease.
Thalassaemia, liver disease or hyposplenism.

steps.x: **A. Auer rods.** Rule: Auer rods = AML; smudge cells = CLL.

technique.stem: A 78 year old man is found to have a lymphocyte count of 14 ×10⁹/L on a routine blood test. Flow cytometry confirms chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. He has no symptoms, no lymphadenopathy and no organomegaly. His haemoglobin and platelets are normal.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate management?

steps.x: Management of confirmed CLL.

clues: Flow cytometry confirms chronic lymphocytic leukaemia
steps.x: Asymptomatic, early stage, normal counts.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Watch and wait**.

elim: Far too toxic for asymptomatic early disease.
For CML, not CLL.
For acute leukaemia; early CLL does not need it.
No splenomegaly and no indication.

steps.x: **E. Watch and wait.** Rule: asymptomatic low-risk CLL = watch and wait.

technique.stem: A 5 year old girl has pallor, bruising and recurrent infections. Her bone marrow is packed with lymphoblasts. Her platelet count is 14 ×10⁹/L.
technique.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of her low platelet count?

steps.x: Mechanism question: explain the finding.
Marrow full of blasts.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Blasts **crowd out** megakaryocytes, so platelets fall.

elim: That is ITP; marrow would have normal megakaryocytes.
Does not explain a marrow packed with blasts.
Not the main mechanism in ALL.
Megaloblastic marrow, not lymphoblasts.

steps.x: **C. Marrow infiltration displacing megakaryocytes.** Rule: leukaemia triad = marrow infiltration displacing normal precursors.

practice.stem: A 3 year old boy has had 2 weeks of pallor, tiredness and bruising. He refuses to walk because his legs hurt. He has cervical lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly. His temperature is 37.9°C, pulse rate 136 bpm and respiratory rate 28 breaths per minute.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Marrow failure, bone pain, lymphadenopathy and HSM with lymphoblasts in a 3 year old is ALL. ITP affects only platelets.

steps.x: Diagnosis of a child with marrow failure.
Peak age, marrow failure triad, bone pain, nodes, HSM; blasts on film.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Mainly over 65s; ALL is the childhood leukaemia.
Only platelets are low; no anaemia, nodes or HSM.
Older child or teenager; no blasts.
Joint swelling, no blasts or pancytopenia.

steps.x: **A. Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia.** Rule: child 2–5 + pancytopenia + blasts + HSM = ALL.

practice.stem: A 69 year old man has 4 weeks of fatigue, breathlessness on exertion, two chest infections and nosebleeds. He has no lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly. The blood film shows myeloblasts containing Auer rods.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: An older adult with marrow failure and Auer rods in myeloblasts has AML. CLL gives smudge cells; CML a massive spleen.

steps.x: Diagnosis from age and film.
Older adult, rapid marrow failure, Auer rods.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Mostly children; no Auer rods.
Slow, often asymptomatic, smudge cells.
Massive splenomegaly and mature myeloid cells.
Teardrop cells and massive splenomegaly.

steps.x: **B. Acute myeloid leukaemia.** Rule: Auer rods = AML.

practice.stem: A 52 year old woman has 3 months of tiredness, night sweats and weight loss of 6 kg. She feels full after small meals. Her spleen is palpable to the right iliac fossa. Her temperature is 37.2°C, pulse rate 88 bpm and BP 124/76 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Massive splenomegaly, a very high WCC with basophils and myeloid cells at all stages is CML. Confirm with BCR-ABL.

steps.x: Diagnosis with a massive spleen.
Constitutional symptoms, early satiety, massive splenomegaly, very high WCC with basophils.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: No blasts dominating; mature cells at all stages.
Lymphocytes, smudge cells, rarely a huge spleen.
Lymphadenopathy, not a huge WCC with basophils.
Young person, sore throat, modest spleen.

steps.x: **C. Chronic myeloid leukaemia.** Rule: massive splenomegaly + huge WCC + basophils = CML.

practice.stem: A 36 year old woman has 1 week of tiredness, heavy bleeding from her gums and large bruises. Her blood film shows abnormal promyelocytes. Cytogenetics show t(15;17). Her pulse rate is 108 bpm and BP 106/64 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: t(15;17) PML-RARA with abnormal promyelocytes and DIC is acute promyelocytic leukaemia.

steps.x: Diagnosis with a translocation.
Bleeding with DIC labs, promyelocytes, t(15;17).

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **APML** (an AML subtype).

elim: Lymphoblasts, not promyelocytes.
Clotting would be normal; no abnormal cells.
Schistocytes and normal clotting times.

steps.x: **B. Acute promyelocytic leukaemia.** Rule: t(15;17) + DIC = APML, a haematological emergency.

practice.stem: A 74 year old man with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia has 2 weeks of increasing tiredness and yellow eyes. His pulse rate is 104 bpm and BP 132/78 mmHg. His direct antiglobulin test is positive.
practice.q: Which is the most likely cause?
o: Bone marrow failure from CLL progression
practice.e: CLL is associated with warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia: haemolysis with a positive DAT.

steps.x: Cause of a new anaemia in CLL.
CLL, jaundice, high reticulocytes and bilirubin, DAT positive.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia**.

elim: Would give low reticulocytes, not haemolysis with a positive DAT.
Linked to mycoplasma and lymphoma; warm AIHA is the classic CLL association.
DAT negative; needs a trigger.
Rapid node growth and systemic illness, not a positive DAT.

steps.x: **E. Warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.** Rule: CLL + haemolysis + DAT positive = warm AIHA.

practice.stem: A 70 year old woman with known chronic lymphocytic leukaemia on watch and wait has rapidly enlarging neck lymph nodes over 3 weeks, fevers, drenching night sweats and weight loss. Her temperature is 38.3°C, pulse rate 102 bpm and BP 118/70 mmHg. LDH is 1100 U/L.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Richter's transformation is CLL becoming high-grade lymphoma: sudden nodal growth, B symptoms and high LDH. It needs a lymph node biopsy.

steps.x: Diagnosis of sudden deterioration in CLL.
Known CLL, rapid nodal growth, B symptoms, very high LDH.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Richter's transformation**.

elim: Marrow failure and Auer rods; not rapid nodal growth.
Causes anaemia and jaundice, not node growth.
CLL progresses slowly; this is sudden.
Possible, but sudden nodal growth, high LDH and B symptoms in CLL point to transformation.

steps.x: **C. Richter's transformation.** Rule: sudden deterioration in CLL = Richter's; confirm with lymph node biopsy.

practice.stem: A 5 year old girl has 3 weeks of bruising, tiredness and fevers. She has hepatosplenomegaly. Her full blood count shows Hb 74 g/L, platelets 30 ×10⁹/L and neutrophils 0.5 ×10⁹/L with blasts on the film. Her pulse rate is 128 bpm.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation?
practice.e: Bone marrow biopsy is the gold standard: it confirms acute leukaemia (at least 20% blasts) and gives the subtype and cytogenetics.

steps.x: Diagnostic (gold-standard) test.
Child with pancytopenia and blasts: suspected acute leukaemia.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Bone marrow biopsy**.

elim: Stages lymphoma; does not diagnose leukaemia.
Gold standard for lymphoma, not leukaemia.
First-line for CLL; marrow is gold standard here.
Already abnormal with blasts; delay is unsafe.

steps.x: **A. Bone marrow biopsy.** Rule: leukaemia gold standard = bone marrow biopsy.

practice.stem: A 72 year old man has a routine blood test before a hernia repair. He is well with no lymphadenopathy.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate initial investigation to confirm the likely diagnosis?
o: CT neck, chest, abdomen and pelvis
practice.e: Flow cytometry of peripheral blood is first-line for CLL, showing a clonal B-cell population. Bone marrow biopsy is not needed first.

steps.x: Initial confirmatory test for the likely diagnosis.
Incidental lymphocytosis with smudge cells in an older man: CLL.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Peripheral blood flow cytometry**.

elim: Not first-line for CLL.
Staging, not diagnosis.
No nodes, and this is for lymphoma.
Screens for myeloma.

steps.x: **D. Peripheral blood flow cytometry.** Rule: CLL is confirmed with flow cytometry of blood.

practice.stem: A 6 year old boy is seen by his GP with 2 weeks of pallor, bruising and bone pain. A same-day full blood count shows blasts. His temperature is 37.4°C, pulse rate 118 bpm and BP 96/60 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate next step in management?
practice.e: NICE: a child with suspected leukaemia is referred the same day to paediatrics. A 2-week wait is too slow.

Child with marrow failure and blasts on film.

practice.stem: A 55 year old man is diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukaemia. He has fatigue and splenomegaly. His pulse rate is 82 bpm and BP 130/82 mmHg. Cytogenetics confirm the Philadelphia chromosome.

practice.stem: A 64 year old woman is 10 days into chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukaemia. She has a temperature of 38.7°C and rigors. Her pulse rate is 118 bpm, BP 96/58 mmHg, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 96% breathing air.

practice.stem: A 48 year old man with chronic myeloid leukaemia starts imatinib. Within 3 months his white cell count and spleen size return to normal.
practice.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of action of imatinib?

practice.e: The t(9;22) BCR-ABL fusion encodes a constitutively active tyrosine kinase; imatinib blocks it.

steps.x: Mechanism of a drug.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Inhibition of the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase**.

elim: That is rituximab.

steps.x: **D. Inhibition of the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase.** Rule: t(9;22) BCR-ABL = constitutive tyrosine kinase = imatinib.
